newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian PM narrowly beats no-confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Estonian PM narrowly beats no-confidence vote.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi narrowly survived a no-confidence vote in parliament on Monday after opposition parties accused him of corruption over apartment privatisations.
The no-confidence motion got the support of 45 of parliament's 101 deputies and 46 voted against it. It needed 51 votes to unseat Vaehi.
"The vote was won and he will continue as prime minister," a spokesman for the prime minister said after the ballot.

Vaehi's heads a minority administration with firm support from 41 deputies and five or six independent deputies backing him from time to time. It is Estonia's fifth government since the small Baltic country quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.

The no-confidence vote was called after several opposition parties said Vaehi helped privatise apartments in the centre of Tallinn in an unethical manner when he was Tallinn council chairman between 1993-1995.
They say he arranged or knew that prime real estate was sold on the cheap and regulations were abused.
Vaehi denied any wrongdoing and said that all privatisations were carried out legally.
